items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I wanted to just follow up on your early life. And you had said your father was a fan of Castro... [INTERVIEWEE] Yes. Like millions of Cubans, they embraced the Cuban revolution... my father was in Castro’s eyes...

ctx.x: I wanted to just follow up on your early life. And you had said your father was a fan of Castro and fought in the Bay of Pigs and embraced the political situation at the time, is that correct?

Yes. Like millions of Cubans, they embraced the Cuban revolution, I mean coming from a poor family so rightfully so my father was in Castro’s eyes because all of the promises that Castro made to the poor Cuban people, talking about equality, inclusion, and so forth and so on. So anyway, yes he did. He fought on Bay of Pigs and then around 1965 he went the opposite way. So he abandoned Castro’s revolution.
What specifically did he get disenchanted with?

items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I always, Monk, since I started using my mind, I’m also I have to say that my dad, who was a huge Fidel Castro fan up to the point that my father fought on Bay of Pigs defending the Cuban regime.

ctx.x: Okay. When you have to go to those lengths to, you know, get an antenna working and pray for the weather and have a good radio set, it makes that music all the much more special because it’s not easily obtained.

Well it was in my case in particular. I cannot talk about all the other musicians. But in my case in particular, Monk, the struggles that I went through in order to listen to that music, to study that music, so forth and so on, made it very very special. Because it was a long struggle about getting your antenna so forth and so on, and also being careful that your neighbor would not hear it, especially that you were listening to. Because you were listening to a radio station from the United States and at that time…
Was jazz in particular sort of banned by the Castro regime? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
